input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view (side-by-side and diff) in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the experiment comparison capability in the Dashboard:
users can select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their
parameters and metrics side by side, with a diff presentation that
highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs.
Today, parameters and metrics live only on per-run pages, forcing data
scientists to compare runs in exported spreadsheets; this epic brings that
comparison into the platform so model promotion decisions have side-by-side
visibility into what changed between candidate runs.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the existing runs list in the
  Dashboard (covering both training runs and pipeline runs).
- A comparison view presenting each selected run's parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- A diff presentation of the comparison that highlights which parameters
  and metrics differ between two selected runs.
- Read-only aggregation of run data already accessible to the Dashboard
  (the same per-run parameters and metrics shown on existing per-run
  pages); no new backend data plane.
- The comparison view is the platform's shared comparison surface: later
  integrations (e.g. opening a comparison from the Model Registry view)
  reuse this view and its run-selection model rather than building a
  second one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list, when the user selects two or more runs, then a
  comparison view opens showing each selected run's parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- Given two selected runs in the comparison view, then the parameters and
  metrics that differ between them are highlighted, and unchanged values
  are distinguishable from changed ones.
- Given runs of both kinds (training runs and pipeline runs), the
  comparison works identically over both — validating that Data Science
  Pipelines run data continues to be consumable through the surfaces the
  Dashboard already uses (Data Science Pipelines is a passive, unchanged
  component in this strategy).
- Given a single selected run, then the comparison entry point is not
  offered (comparison requires two or more runs).
- The comparison view renders successfully for runs with differing
  parameter/metric sets (values present on one run and absent on another
  are shown as such, not as errors).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: Users can select two or more runs and view their
  parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard — the side-by-side
  comparison view and runs-list multi-select.
- **HLR-3 (P1)**: Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which
  parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs — the diff
  presentation of the same comparison surface, consolidated into this epic
  with HLR-1 (one capability, one surface, higher priority P0).

# Producing-run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: a registered model
version records a reference to the run that produced it, so the lineage is
part of the registry's model-version metadata and can be used to open a
comparison of the producing run from registry-facing surfaces. The Model
Registry is the source of truth linking model versions to their training
lineage; this epic makes the producing run a resolvable part of that
record.

## Scope

- Define how a registered model version carries a reference to the run
  that produced it (the architecture context documents custom properties
  on model versions as the extension point for structured metadata; the
  concrete mechanism is an implementation decision for the Model Registry
  team).
- Record the producing-run reference when a model version is registered
  from a run, including validation that the reference resolves to a run
  in the same project.
- Expose the producing-run reference through the Model Registry REST API
  so Dashboard and other clients can read it.
- Preserve compatibility: existing registered model versions without a
  producing-run reference remain valid, and existing registration flows
  keep working.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered with a producing run, then the model
  version's metadata includes a reference to that run, retrievable
  through the Model Registry REST API.
- Given a producing-run reference on a model version, then the reference
  resolves to the run that produced it within the same project.
- Given a model version registered without run information, then
  registration succeeds and the model version remains valid (the
  producing-run reference is optional and backward compatible).
- The lineage reference is specified and documented precisely enough for
  a consuming UI to resolve the run and its parameters/metrics (the
  contract the registry-side comparison entry point builds against).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Registered model versions link back to the run that
  produced them — the registry-side half (lineage data recorded on model
  versions and exposed via the REST API); the "comparison can be opened
  from the Model Registry" half is delivered by the Dashboard-side
  registry entry point.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry view

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry entry point to run comparison in the
Dashboard: the registry's model-version view surfaces the run that
produced a registered model version (from the lineage reference recorded
in the Model Registry) and lets the user open the run comparison view with
that run pre-selected, so a comparison can be started directly from the
Model Registry without first finding the run in the runs list. The
registry UI lives in the Dashboard, so this is Dashboard work building on
two prerequisites: the run-comparison capability and the producing-run
lineage on model versions.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry view, display the producing run of a
  registered model version, read from the lineage reference exposed
  through the Model Registry REST API.
- Provide an action from a model version that opens the run comparison
  view with the linked producing run pre-selected, letting the user add
  further runs to the comparison.
- Graceful degradation: for model versions without a producing-run
  reference, the lineage display and comparison entry point are hidden or
  disabled without errors.
- Reuse the platform's run comparison view and its run-selection model —
  no second comparison surface is built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a producing-run reference, then
  the registry view in the Dashboard shows the producing run.
- Given a registered model version with a producing-run reference, when
  the user opens the comparison from that model version, then the run
  comparison view opens with the linked run pre-selected and further runs
  can be added to the comparison.
- Given a model version without a producing-run reference, then the
  registry view renders normally with the comparison entry point hidden
  or disabled (no errors, no dead links).
- The comparison opened from the registry behaves identically to the
  comparison opened from the runs list (same view, same side-by-side and
  diff behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: "...so a comparison can be opened from the Model
  Registry" — the Dashboard-side half of HLR-2 (registry UI entry point);
  the lineage-on-model-versions half is delivered by the Model Registry
  epic.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic documents the run comparison workflow end to end in the product
documentation: how users compare training and pipeline runs side by side
starting from the runs list, how to read the diff highlighting of changed
parameters and metrics, and how to open a comparison from the Model
Registry via a model version's producing-run link. Documentation is
written after the implementation is complete so it describes what was
actually built.

## Scope

- A documentation topic (or topics) covering the comparison workflow
  started from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters/metrics view, and interpreting the diff
  highlighting between two selected runs.
- A documentation section covering the workflow started from the Model
  Registry: viewing a model version's producing run and opening a
  comparison from it, including the behavior when a model version has no
  producing-run reference.
- Screenshots and procedures consistent with the implemented Dashboard
  and Model Registry behavior.
- Cross-links between the runs/comparison topics and the Model Registry
  topics so both entry points are discoverable from each other.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers starting a comparison from the runs
  list, including multi-run selection and reading the side-by-side and
  diff views.
- Published documentation covers starting a comparison from the Model
  Registry via a model version's producing-run link.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented comparison
  capability and registry integration (reviewed by engineering against
  the actual behavior, with discrepancies resolved).
- Screenshots and procedure steps match the shipped UI.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both
  the runs list and the registry — full coverage of this HLR. Epic
  priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy
  priority Major → P1).
